from __future__ import annotations

from io import BytesIO

import pytest

from telegram import (
    Animation,
    Audio,
    Document,
    InputMediaAnimation,
    InputMediaAudio,
    InputMediaDocument,
    InputMediaPhoto,
    InputMediaVideo,
    InputPaidMediaPhoto,
    InputPaidMediaVideo,
    InputSticker,
    PhotoSize,
    Video,
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "case_id",
    [
        "photo_bytes",
        "photo_io",
        "photo_local_path",
        "photo_file_uri",
        "photo_remote_string",
        "photo_photosize_obj",
        "video_bytes_thumb_bytes",
        "video_io_thumb_io",
        "video_local_path_thumb_local_path",
        "video_video_obj",
        "animation_bytes_thumb_bytes",
        "animation_obj_thumb_io",
        "audio_bytes_thumb_bytes",
        "audio_obj_thumb_local_path",
        "document_obj_thumb_io",
        "document_io_thumb_file_uri",
        "paid_photo_bytes",
        "paid_video_io_thumb_uri",
        "sticker_bytes",
        "sticker_local_path",
    ],
)
def test_inputmedia_parse_file_input_line_coverage_suite(case_id: str, tmp_path) -> None:
    media_file = tmp_path / "media_payload.bin"
    media_file.write_bytes(b"payload-123")
    local_path = str(media_file)
    file_uri = media_file.resolve().as_uri()

    if case_id == "photo_bytes":
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media=b"photo-bytes", caption="c")
    elif case_id == "photo_io":
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media=BytesIO(b"photo-io"))
    elif case_id == "photo_local_path":
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media=local_path)
    elif case_id == "photo_file_uri":
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media=file_uri)
    elif case_id == "photo_remote_string":
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media="AgACAgQAAxkBAAICV2")
    elif case_id == "photo_photosize_obj":
        photo_obj = PhotoSize(
            file_id="photo_file_id_01",
            file_unique_id="uniq_photo_01",
            width=17,
            height=23,
        )
        obj = InputMediaPhoto(media=photo_obj)
    elif case_id == "video_bytes_thumb_bytes":
        obj = InputMediaVideo(media=b"video-bytes", thumbnail=b"thumb-bytes")
    elif case_id == "video_io_thumb_io":
        obj = InputMediaVideo(media=BytesIO(b"video-io"), thumbnail=BytesIO(b"thumb-io"))
    elif case_id == "video_local_path_thumb_local_path":
        obj = InputMediaVideo(media=local_path, thumbnail=local_path)
    elif case_id == "video_video_obj":
        video_obj = Video(
            file_id="video_file_id_01",
            file_unique_id="uniq_video_01",
            width=320,
            height=180,
            duration=11,
        )
        obj = InputMediaVideo(media=video_obj, thumbnail="http://example.com/t.jpg")
    elif case_id == "animation_bytes_thumb_bytes":
        obj = InputMediaAnimation(media=b"anim-bytes", thumbnail=b"anim-thumb")
    elif case_id == "animation_obj_thumb_io":
        animation_obj = Animation(
            file_id="anim_file_id_01",
            file_unique_id="uniq_anim_01",
            width=100,
            height=60,
            duration=4,
        )
        obj = InputMediaAnimation(media=animation_obj, thumbnail=BytesIO(b"anim-thumb-io"))
    elif case_id == "audio_bytes_thumb_bytes":
        obj = InputMediaAudio(media=b"audio-bytes", thumbnail=b"audio-thumb")
    elif case_id == "audio_obj_thumb_local_path":
        audio_obj = Audio(
            file_id="audio_file_id_01",
            file_unique_id="uniq_audio_01",
            duration=7,
            performer="ptb",
            title="qa",
        )
        obj = InputMediaAudio(media=audio_obj, thumbnail=local_path)
    elif case_id == "document_obj_thumb_io":
        document_obj = Document(
            file_id="doc_file_id_01",
            file_unique_id="uniq_doc_01",
            file_name="x.txt",
        )
        obj = InputMediaDocument(media=document_obj, thumbnail=BytesIO(b"doc-thumb"))
    elif case_id == "document_io_thumb_file_uri":
        obj = InputMediaDocument(media=BytesIO(b"doc-io"), thumbnail="file:///tmp/doc-thumb.jpg")
    elif case_id == "paid_photo_bytes":
        obj = InputPaidMediaPhoto(media=b"paid-photo")
    elif case_id == "paid_video_io_thumb_uri":
        obj = InputPaidMediaVideo(media=BytesIO(b"paid-video"), thumbnail="file:///tmp/paid-thumb.png")
    elif case_id == "sticker_bytes":
        obj = InputSticker(sticker=b"sticker-bytes", emoji_list=["🙂"], format="static")
    elif case_id == "sticker_local_path":
        obj = InputSticker(sticker=local_path, emoji_list=["🙂"], format="video")
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected case_id: {case_id}")

    assert obj is not None

79	def is_local_file(obj: Optional[FilePathInput]) -> bool:
80	    """
81	    Checks if a given string is a file on local system.
82	
83	    Args:
84	        obj (:obj:`str`): The string to check.
85	    """
86	    if obj is None:
87	        return False
88	
89	    path = Path(obj)
90	    try:
91	        return path.is_file()
92	    except Exception:
93	        return False

96	def parse_file_input(  # pylint: disable=too-many-return-statements
97	    file_input: Union[FileInput, "TelegramObject"],
98	    tg_type: Optional[type["TelegramObject"]] = None,
99	    filename: Optional[str] = None,
100	    attach: bool = False,
101	    local_mode: bool = False,
102	) -> Union[str, "InputFile", Any]:
103	    """
104	    Parses input for sending files:
105	
106	    * For string input, if the input is an absolute path of a local file:
107	
108	        * if ``local_mode`` is ``True``, adds the ``file://`` prefix. If the input is a relative
109	        path of a local file, computes the absolute path and adds the ``file://`` prefix.
110	        * if ``local_mode`` is ``False``, loads the file as binary data and builds an
111	          :class:`InputFile` from that
112	
113	      Returns the input unchanged, otherwise.
114	    * :class:`pathlib.Path` objects are treated the same way as strings.
115	    * For IO and bytes input, returns an :class:`telegram.InputFile`.
116	    * If :attr:`tg_type` is specified and the input is of that type, returns the ``file_id``
117	      attribute.
118	
119	    Args:
120	        file_input (:obj:`str` | :obj:`bytes` | :term:`file object` | :class:`~telegram.InputFile`\
121	            | Telegram media object): The input to parse.
122	        tg_type (:obj:`type`, optional): The Telegram media type the input can be. E.g.
123	            :class:`telegram.Animation`.
124	        filename (:obj:`str`, optional): The filename. Only relevant in case an
125	            :class:`telegram.InputFile` is returned.
126	        attach (:obj:`bool`, optional): Pass :obj:`True` if the parameter this file belongs to in
127	            the request to Telegram should point to the multipart data via an ``attach://`` URI.
128	            Defaults to `False`. Only relevant if an :class:`telegram.InputFile` is returned.
129	        local_mode (:obj:`bool`, optional): Pass :obj:`True` if the bot is running an api server
130	            in ``--local`` mode.
131	
132	    Returns:
133	        :obj:`str` | :class:`telegram.InputFile` | :obj:`object`: The parsed input or the untouched
134	        :attr:`file_input`, in case it's no valid file input.
135	    """
136	    # Importing on file-level yields cyclic Import Errors
137	    from telegram import InputFile  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
138	
139	    if isinstance(file_input, str) and file_input.startswith("file://"):
140	        if not local_mode:
141	            raise ValueError("Specified file input is a file URI, but local mode is not enabled.")
142	        return file_input
143	    if isinstance(file_input, (str, Path)):
144	        if is_local_file(file_input):
145	            path = Path(file_input)
146	            if local_mode:
147	                return path.absolute().as_uri()
148	            return InputFile(path.open(mode="rb"), filename=filename, attach=attach)
149	
150	        return file_input
151	    if isinstance(file_input, bytes):
152	        return InputFile(file_input, filename=filename, attach=attach)
153	    if hasattr(file_input, "read"):
154	        return InputFile(cast(IO, file_input), filename=filename, attach=attach)
155	    if tg_type and isinstance(file_input, tg_type):
156	        return file_input.file_id  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
157	    return file_input
158

I wrote the answer file. I worked it out by reading the code, not by running the tests, which this environment doesn't allow.

```json
{"covered_lines": [137, 139, 142, 143, 144, 145, 146, 147, 150, 151, 152, 153, 154, 155, 156]}
```

The key fact is that every constructor in `inputmedia.py` and `inputsticker.py` calls `parse_file_input` with `local_mode=True`. That decides which branch each test case takes:

- **`file://` inputs** (the photo file URI and the `file:///tmp/...` thumbnails) return at line 142, so line 141 (the `ValueError`) is never reached.
- **Existing local paths** go through 143 → 144 → 145 → 146 and return a `file://` URI at 147, so line 148 (opening the file) is never reached.
